description.p: Moriartty is a fast, private-by-default terminal emulator inspired by PuTTY's pterm. It keeps PuTTY's habits — copy on select, right-click paste and the familiar configuration tree — in a native GTK 4 application, with no network access and no telemetry.

ul.li: Copy on select and right-click paste, on by default
Safe paste: escape sequences and hidden control characters are stripped, multi-line pastes ask first
Tabs, find in scrollback, font zoom and Ctrl+click web links
Moriartty Dark and Light colours that follow the desktop, plus PuTTY classic, Tango, Solarized and Dracula
Saved settings profiles and session logging
New Moriartty Dark and Light colours that follow the desktop's light or dark style
The title bar matches the terminal's colours
Tabs can be dragged to reorder them and scrolled with the mouse wheel
More room around the text, and optional background transparency
Colour changes are previewed live in the settings window
Sharper, square application icons
Selected text no longer goes to the clipboard unless you turn that on; right-click still pastes it
Hyperlinks set by programs and international web addresses ask before opening
Links with hidden characters are refused
Pastes with hidden characters are shown before they are sent
Copying a large scrollback asks first
A tab shows when its output is being logged
Unreadable saved settings are kept aside instead of being overwritten

description.p: The close button on a tab works again.

ul.li: Much slimmer title bar
Double-clicking the title bar no longer also opens a tab
One slim title bar with the tabs in it
Click next to the tabs for a new tab; middle-click closes one
Tabs are named after what runs in them
Tab shortcuts work wherever the keyboard focus is
Tabs, with keyboard shortcuts for opening, closing, switching and moving them
A broken saved shell or log file setting no longer stops Moriartty from starting
Safer paste confirmation: Cancel is the default and hidden characters are shown
Links that hide their real host behind a user name are refused
Link tooltips reveal the real host of international domain names
The Event Log updates live
Hardened log file and pseudo-terminal handling
Can be chosen as the desktop's default terminal (xdg-terminal-exec, x-terminal-emulator)
New -dir and -hold options
Font zoom is remembered and can be saved as default
Option to hide the title bar buttons
Closing a window running an -e program now asks first
The terminal now resizes without polling

description.p: Find in scrollback, font zoom, Ctrl+click links, colour schemes, settings saved as default.
